prompt: A security review found that routes/visit-notes.js builds the HTML response by concatenating note_text straight into the page without escaping it, so a stored XSS payload in a note would execute for anyone who views that care recipient's notes. I already know the fix is to escape/encode the output. Can you write a test that proves notes can't inject script into the page?

assertions.text: Test is written in a real, runnable framework, not Gherkin/BDD prose
assertions.evidence_hint: an actual test file using a real test runner syntax

assertions.text: Test sends an XSS payload as note_text and checks it is not rendered as executable markup (escaped/encoded in output)
assertions.evidence_hint: a script-tag or event-handler payload asserted to be neutralized in the response body

assertions.text: The test actually ran in this session, with real pass/fail output shown, not just claimed
assertions.evidence_hint: a command and its real output

assertions.text: States what's being tested (the seam) explicitly before or alongside the code, not just code with no framing
assertions.evidence_hint: a one-line statement of what the test checks

assertions.text: Names the attack (stored XSS / script injection) and the structural control (output encoding/escaping) explicitly, not just 'add validation'
assertions.evidence_hint: explicit naming of both the attack and the fix mechanism
